title: Man who stopped Oregon elementary school shooter is father of 2 students, his mom says
summary: The man who stopped a deadly elementary school attack in Oregon by shooting the teenage gunman inside the building is the father of two girls at the school, his mother said Friday.

image.caption: Kyle Ketchum, right, embraces Christina Edwards at a makeshift memorial outside Silver Rail Elementary in Bend, Ore., on Friday, a day after the deadly shooting. (Joe Kline/The Associated Press)

blocks.text: World·New
The man who stopped a deadly elementary school attack in Oregon by shooting the teenage gunman inside the building is the father of two girls at the school, his mother said Friday.
Police said suspect was killed by someone who followed him into school
The man who stopped a deadly elementary school attack in Oregon by shooting the teenage gunman inside the building is the father of two girls who attend the school, his mother said Friday.
In a statement read to reporters Friday, Kenda Freeman said her son, Kaylub Giamanco, intervened in Thursday's attack at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend and shot the teenage shooter.
Three students and a teacher were killed in the attack, and a fourth student and another teacher were critically injured.

"He is not seeking recognition, but instead wishes to express his gratitude to the first responders, school personnel and community for the outpouring of love and support," Freeman said, noting that her son is a lifelong resident of Bend, a mountain-ringed city of about 100,000 in central Oregon that has grown quickly in recent decades.
Police have not yet identified who shot the gunman, only saying that the suspect was found dead inside the school minutes after the shooting was first reported. They also haven't named the gunman.

At a news conference hours after Thursday's attack, Gov. Tina Kotek — without naming him —praised Giamanco for following the gunman into the school, saying he helped end the rampage and likely saved lives as police began arriving on the scene.

"To the community member who heroically intervened to stop further loss of life: Your actions carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well," said Kotek.
A makeshift memorial at a sign marking the Silver Rail Elementary School near a cordoned-off area in Bend, Ore., on Thursday. (David Ryder/Reuters)
Memorials of flowers, balloons and stuffed animals appeared around the school, which sits in a densely packed neighbourhood filled with newly built homes.
Brooke Olsen, whose daughter is a kindergartner at Silver Rail, said she was amazed that a member of the public pursued the shooter.
"I think it's miraculous that someone was there before law enforcement even arrived to stop further tragedy from happening," Olsen said Friday, weeping at times. "I'm feeling very grateful."

items: 3 children, 1 teacher dead after shooting at Oregon elementary school, police say

blocks.text: Shooter used gun bought by his mom

The 16-year-old suspect, identified only as a Bend resident, was found dead inside the school minutes after the first calls for help, Police Chief Mike Krantz said. Police said he got into the school by shooting through locked doors.

The children who were killed were ages five, eight and 11 years old, Krantz said. Authorities did not give details about the teacher who was killed. Another seven-year-old child and a 54-year-old teacher were wounded in the attack and taken to hospital in critical condition, he said.

The attacker used a pump-action shotgun that was purchased by his mother, according to a law enforcement official briefed on the shooting. The official spoke to The Associated Press on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to publicly discuss the investigation.
Under Oregon law, a minor may possess a shotgun if it is provided by a parent or by someone else with the parent's consent.
Police said they didn't know if the shooter knew anyone at the school or if he had attended it.
An officer stands behind police tape that surrounds Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Ore., where a shooting took place, on Thursday. (Joe Kline/The Associated Press)

The first 911 call came early in the afternoon from someone outside the school who reported being shot at by someone with a long gun, the police chief said. More 911 calls came from inside the school, and officers arrived within minutes, police spokesperson Sheila Miller said.
The attacker was shot and went down inside the school shortly after officers arrived, she said.
The school serves students from kindergarten through Grade 5, with about 450 enrolled last year, according to the Oregon Department of Education.

Children were taken by bus to a nearby church serving as a reunification centre for families. Parents hugged, kissed and held their kids' hands as they walked to their cars, with some bringing along favourite stuffed animals or other comfort items from home.
A community grieves
Shaken residents held a vigil Thursday night, where children drew hearts in chalk on the sidewalk and held candles side-by-side with adults.
Classes and all other activities were cancelled Friday for the area's 32 schools.

Dara Crawford cries during a candlelight vigil at Drake Park following a deadly shooting at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Ore. on Thursday. (Eli Imadali/Oregon Public Broadcasting/The Associated Press)

Bend, the largest city in central Oregon, is about 125 miles (200 kilometres) southeast of Portland. It's population has grown rapidly over the past three decades, and it is a tourism and outdoor recreation hub.
The shooting was the 28th mass killing in the U.S. this year, according to a database maintained by The Associated Press and USA Today in partnership with Northeastern University.

Four years ago in Bend, a grocery store employee who had served in the U.S. Army confronted a gunman who was firing inside the supermarket. Both the employee, whom police hailed as a hero, and a customer were killed. The gunman died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
